subject: [AMBER] cpptraj warnings topology flags being ignored

messages.author: Vaibhav Dixit
messages.body:

messages.author: David A Case
messages.body:
On Thu, Dec 17, 2020, Vaibhav Dixit wrote:
>Warning: Amber topology flag 'CMAP_COUNT' is unrecognized and will be
>skipped.
These are innocuous: cpptraj doesn't have any actions that are specific
to CMAP force field terms, and just skips data it doesn't know about.
Dan: I think these warnings (and there are many of them) might just be
skipped.  Since there are no CMAP-specific actions (that I know of!), I
don't think users will be misled if cpptraj just silently skipped.
We want to focus users' attention on the more important warnings and
errors.
....dac

messages.author: Daniel Roe
messages.body:
Hi,
Just use a more up-to-date version of cpptraj and it will properly
read and write these flags.
On Thu, Dec 17, 2020 at 11:35 AM David A Case <david.case.rutgers.edu> wrote:
>
> On Thu, Dec 17, 2020, Vaibhav Dixit wrote:
> Dan: I think these warnings (and there are many of them) might just be
> skipped.  Since there are no CMAP-specific actions (that I know of!), I
> don't think users will be misled if cpptraj just silently skipped.
> We want to focus users' attention on the more important warnings and
> errors.
I think these are important warnings, particularly if users are using
commands like 'strip', 'parmstrip', 'closest' etc to write out new
topology files; they should be aware that the older version of cpptraj
is not including those terms.
-Dan
